comparison: Aquadactyl v1.3-beta vs Pterodactyl v1.15.2 vs Pterodactyl v2.0.0-beta.3

methodology.fixture: One non-admin user owning 50 suspended server records, one node, one nest, one egg, one allocation per server. No Wings calls or running game containers in the measured stacks.
methodology.sharedConfiguration: PHP 8.4, four static FPM workers, OPcache 128 MiB, PHP memory_limit 256 MiB; nginx one worker with gzip level 6; config/route/view caches; one queue worker. Each panel 2 CPU quota cores/1 GiB; each MariaDB 1 core/512 MiB; each Redis 0.5 core/128 MiB. REDIS_CLIENT=phpredis on all three. Production mode, debug and telemetry off, no extra addons.
methodology.browser: Headless Chromium, 1440x900, deviceScaleFactor 1, no CPU or network throttling, localhost Docker port forwarding. One warm-up pair discarded; ten measured pairs per panel in rotating order. Cold uses a new context restored from an authenticated session; warm reloads the same page/context. Server/OS caches remain warm. Wait for the first visible fixture server row, then 2 seconds to observe paints. The dashboard uses each release's normal pagination; visible row counts are recorded. Third-party requests are blocked identically to isolate the local panel; blocked URLs are recorded. FCP/LCP are navigation-to-paint; dashboardReady is measured when a fixture server name first appears visibly in the viewport, a custom application milestone. Heap is CDP JSHeapUsedSize after an explicit garbage collection; not total browser RAM.
methodology.api: GET /api/client/account and GET /api/client?per_page=50, valid user API key, HTTP/1.1 persistent connections, uncompressed response bodies, concurrency 1/8/16; 10-second closed-loop windows, three repetitions with rotating panel order. Two-second warm-up before each run. No new requests after the window, in-flight requests drained and included in elapsed time. Validate every HTTP status and JSON result. Rate limits raised to 1,000,000/min on all three disposable panels. Successes per actual elapsed second, not offered requests per second or a maximum capacity claim.
methodology.memory: cgroup v2 memory.current minus inactive_file, clamped to zero (Docker-style working set). Separately retain raw usage bytes. Ten 1-second-spaced samples per window, three windows each after warm-up, idle and during concurrency-16 server-list load. Each sample records panel, database and Redis, and their sum. Peak is the maximum observed sample, not the kernel high-water mark. No application restarts or forced PHP GC between windows. Browser heap and server working set are different metrics.
methodology.limitations: Single shared Windows/WSL2 workstation; existing unrelated application containers remain running. No CPU pinning, controlled network emulation, TLS, WAN latency, mobile device, endurance test or real-player load. This is a controlled local configuration comparison of pinned distributions, not their default deployment presets or proof of general production capacity.
